The wave redirecting system includes a lower frame body having a first upper surface and a second upper surface. The lower frame body provides a base structure for the system and is configured to support additional components of the wave redirecting assembly.

The system further includes an upper frame body that is connected to, or formed integrally with, the lower frame body. The upper frame body extends relative to the lower frame body and is arranged so that it forms a first angle and a second angle with the lower frame body. These angular relationships help define the overall geometry of the wave redirecting system and may contribute to the manner in which incoming wave energy is received, guided, or redirected.

A plurality of anchor feet are connected to, or formed integrally with, a bottom surface of the lower frame body. The anchor feet are configured to engage with a supporting surface, such as a seabed, floor, or other installation surface, to help stabilize and secure the wave redirecting system in position during use.

The system also includes a redirecting blade connected to, or formed integrally with, the upper frame body. The redirecting blade is positioned so that it forms a third angle with the upper frame body. This angled arrangement allows the redirecting blade to interact with incoming waves and redirect at least a portion of the wave energy in a desired direction. Together, the lower frame body, upper frame body, anchor feet, and redirecting blade cooperate to provide a structurally supported wave redirecting system.
outputs.L4:
A wave redirecting system is provided for controlling, guiding, or altering the movement of wave energy in a body of water. The system includes a structural frame assembly formed from a lower frame body and an upper frame body that are connected together and arranged at multiple angles relative to one another. By using angled frame sections, the system presents a shaped surface profile to incoming waves, allowing wave energy to be intercepted and redirected rather than passing through the area in an uncontrolled manner.

The lower frame body forms a base portion of the system and is configured to rest on, engage with, or be positioned adjacent to an underwater or shoreline support surface. One or more anchor feet are provided on the lower frame body to stabilize the system during use. These anchor feet help maintain the position of the frame assembly against forces produced by moving water, wave impact, current, or shifting sediment. The anchor feet may be shaped or arranged to improve gripping, load distribution, or resistance to sliding and overturning.

The upper frame body is connected to the lower frame body and extends upwardly at one or more selected angles. The angular relationship between the lower and upper frame bodies helps define the direction in which wave energy is redirected. The upper frame body supports a redirecting blade, which is mounted to the frame in a position where it can contact or influence incoming water movement. The blade may extend along a portion of the upper frame body and may be angled, curved, or otherwise shaped to guide water flow in a desired direction.

During operation, waves approaching the system encounter the lower frame body, the upper frame body, and the redirecting blade. The angled structural surfaces and the blade cooperate to change the direction, distribution, or intensity of the wave movement. Instead of allowing wave energy to travel directly forward, the system redirects at least a portion of that energy along a different path, upwardly, laterally, downwardly, or away from a protected area, depending on the selected configuration.

The connected frame bodies provide structural support for the blade and help transfer wave loads through the system to the anchor feet and supporting surface. This arrangement creates a stable anchored structure capable of withstanding repeated wave action while maintaining the desired orientation of the redirecting blade. As a result, the system may be used to manage wave movement near shorelines, docks, marine structures, erosion-prone areas, or other locations where controlling wave energy is beneficial.
outputs.L5:
**A Wave Redirecting**

A wave redirecting is a powerful image of movement, change, and adaptation. Whether it is an ocean wave meeting a rocky shore, a sound wave bouncing off a wall, or a light wave bending as it passes through glass, redirection shows how energy does not simply disappear when it meets an obstacle. Instead, it changes direction, form, or path.

In nature, waves are constantly being redirected. Ocean waves curve around islands, crash against cliffs, and flow into new channels. Wind can push them one way, while the shape of the seabed guides them another. This redirection can be gentle, like ripples spreading across a pond, or forceful, like storm waves reshaping a coastline.

The idea of a wave redirecting can also be used as a metaphor. People often face obstacles that force them to change direction. Like a wave, we may not be able to continue on the same path, but we can still move forward. Redirection is not always failure; sometimes it is the beginning of a new route, a new purpose, or a better outcome.

In science, wave redirection is important in many fields. Mirrors redirect light waves, satellites redirect radio waves, and acoustic panels redirect sound waves. Engineers and designers use this principle to improve communication, build safer structures, and create clearer sound environments.

A wave redirecting reminds us that energy is resilient. It may be blocked, bent, reflected, or transformed, but it continues to move. In both the physical world and human life, redirection is a natural part of progress.

counterfactuals.output:
Below is sample patent-application-style wording for a wave deflector structure.

---

## Title

**Wave Deflector Structure Having Lower Frame, Angled Upper Frame, Anchoring Feet, and Redirecting Blade**

## Abstract

A wave deflector structure includes a lower frame configured to rest on or adjacent to a support surface, an upper frame connected to the lower frame and extending at an angle relative thereto, a plurality of anchoring feet connected to the lower frame, and a redirecting blade supported by the upper frame. The redirecting blade includes a wave-facing surface configured to receive incident wave energy and redirect at least a portion of the wave energy upwardly, laterally, or back toward an incoming wave direction. The lower frame, upper frame, anchoring feet, and redirecting blade may be integrally formed or connected by mechanical fasteners, welding, bonding, or other joining structures. The structure is adapted for placement along a shoreline, seawall, dock, pier, flood barrier, or other wave-exposed installation.

---

## Field

The present disclosure relates generally to wave attenuation and redirection structures, and more particularly to a wave deflector structure having a lower frame, an angled upper frame, anchoring feet, and a blade or deflecting surface arranged to redirect incident water or wave energy.

---

## Background

Shoreline structures, waterfront barriers, docks, piers, and coastal installations may be subjected to repeated wave impact. Conventional barriers may absorb wave energy through mass or may present a substantially vertical surface to incoming waves. Such arrangements can result in reflected wave energy, splash, overtopping, erosion at the base of the structure, or undesirable loading on adjacent structures.

There is a need for a wave deflector structure that can be anchored relative to a support surface and that includes a blade or deflecting surface positioned at an angle to redirect incident wave energy. There is also a need for a structure that may be modular, connected to other similar structures, and configured for installation on different support surfaces.

---

## Summary

In one embodiment, a wave deflector structure includes a lower frame having a first end, a second end, an upper surface, a lower surface, and opposing side surfaces. An upper frame is connected to the lower frame and extends upwardly from the lower frame at an oblique angle. The upper frame may include a lower end connected to the lower frame and an upper end spaced from the lower frame. A redirecting blade is connected to or supported by the upper frame. The redirecting blade has a front surface configured to face incoming waves, a rear surface opposite the front surface, a lower blade end, an upper blade end, and opposing lateral blade ends. The front surface of the redirecting blade is oriented to deflect wave energy away from the lower frame.

In another embodiment, a plurality of anchoring feet are connected to the lower frame. Each anchoring foot may include a body portion extending outwardly from the lower frame and a bottom surface configured to engage a support surface. Each anchoring foot may include one or more apertures configured to receive an anchor, pile, fastener, rod, stake, bolt, or other securing member.

In some embodiments, the lower frame, upper frame, anchoring feet, and redirecting blade are formed as a unitary or integral structure. In other embodiments, one or more of the lower frame, upper frame, anchoring feet, and redirecting blade are separately formed and connected together. The connected components may be joined by welding, bolting, clamping, adhesive bonding, molding, casting, interlocking engagement, or any combination thereof.

---

## Detailed Description

A wave deflector structure may include a base or lower frame configured to be positioned on a ground surface, bed surface, concrete surface, dock surface, shoreline surface, seabed, riverbed, lakebed, or other support surface. The lower frame may define a generally elongate body extending between a first lower-frame end and a second lower-frame end. The lower frame may further include a top surface, a bottom surface, a front side surface, and a rear side surface. The bottom surface may be substantially planar, contoured, ribbed, serrated, or otherwise configured to engage the support surface.

An upper frame is connected to the lower frame. The upper frame may extend from the lower frame at an acute or obtuse angle relative to the lower frame. In some embodiments, the upper frame extends upwardly and rearwardly from a front portion of the lower frame. In other embodiments, the upper frame extends upwardly and forwardly from a rear portion of the lower frame. The upper frame may include a lower upper-frame end connected to the lower frame and an opposite upper upper-frame end spaced vertically above the lower frame.

The upper frame may include one or more support members. For example, the upper frame may include first and second side support members extending upwardly from the lower frame, a transverse upper member extending between upper ends of the side support members, and one or more intermediate braces extending between the lower frame and the upper frame. The support members may define a blade-supporting plane oriented at an angle relative to the lower frame.

A redirecting blade is supported by the upper frame. The redirecting blade may be connected to a wave-facing side of the upper frame, a rear side of the upper frame, or may be received within a channel, groove, slot, or bracket defined by the upper frame. The redirecting blade may include a front wave-engaging surface and an opposite rear surface. The front wave-engaging surface may be substantially planar, concave, convex, curved, faceted, ribbed, or provided with flow-directing features. The blade may further include a lower end positioned adjacent to or above the lower frame, an upper end positioned adjacent the upper end of the upper frame, and first and second lateral ends extending between the lower and upper ends.

The redirecting blade is oriented such that water contacting the front surface of the blade is redirected along the front surface toward the upper end, toward a lateral end, or back away from the support surface. In certain embodiments, the front surface of the blade is inclined relative to a vertical direction to reduce direct impact loading and to convert a portion of incoming wave energy into redirected flow.

Anchoring feet are connected to the lower frame. Each anchoring foot may project laterally, longitudinally, downwardly, or a combination thereof from the lower frame. Each anchoring foot may include an upper foot surface, a bottom foot surface, an outer foot end spaced from the lower frame, and an inner foot end connected to or integrally formed with the lower frame. One or more anchor apertures may extend between the upper foot surface and the bottom foot surface. The anchor apertures may be sized to receive anchors for securing the wave deflector structure to a substrate.

In some embodiments, the anchoring feet are disposed at or near the first and second ends of the lower frame. In other embodiments, additional anchoring feet are positioned between the first and second ends. The anchoring feet may extend forwardly of the lower frame, rearwardly of the lower frame, laterally from the lower frame, or symmetrically about the lower frame. The anchoring feet may be fixed to the lower frame by welding, bolts, gussets, brackets, integral molding, casting, additive manufacturing, or other structural connection methods.

The lower frame and upper frame may be connected by one or more gussets or braces. A brace may include a first brace end connected to the lower frame and a second brace end connected to the upper frame. The brace may extend along a diagonal path and may resist bending of the upper frame under wave impact. The gussets may be positioned adjacent lateral ends of the structure, adjacent intermediate portions of the structure, or along a rear side of the blade.

The wave deflector structure may be formed from metal, reinforced polymer, composite, concrete, fiberglass, high-density polyethylene, marine-grade aluminum, stainless steel, coated steel, or combinations thereof. In some embodiments, the redirecting blade is formed from a corrosion-resistant plate or panel. In other embodiments, the redirecting blade is formed integrally with the upper frame.

A plurality of wave deflector structures may be arranged end-to-end. The first lower-frame end may include a first connector and the second lower-frame end may include a complementary second connector. The first and second connectors may permit adjacent wave deflector structures to be joined in a linear, curved, angled, or articulated arrangement. The lateral ends of adjacent redirecting blades may overlap, abut, interlock, or be spaced apart.

---

## Example Claims

### Claim 1

A wave deflector structure comprising:

a lower frame having a first lower-frame end, a second lower-frame end, an upper lower-frame surface, a lower lower-frame surface, and opposing lower-frame side surfaces;

an upper frame connected to the lower frame, the upper frame having a lower upper-frame end connected to the lower frame and an upper upper-frame end spaced from the lower frame, the upper frame extending at an oblique angle relative to the lower frame;

a plurality of anchoring feet connected to the lower frame, each anchoring foot having an inner foot end connected to the lower frame, an outer foot end spaced from the lower frame, and a bottom foot surface configured to engage a support surface; and

a redirecting blade connected to the upper frame, the redirecting blade having a front wave-facing surface, a rear surface opposite the front wave-facing surface, a lower blade end, an upper blade end, and opposing lateral blade ends,

wherein the front wave-facing surface of the redirecting blade is oriented at an angle relative to the lower frame to redirect incident wave energy away from the lower frame.

### Claim 2

The wave deflector structure of claim 1, wherein the lower frame, the upper frame, the plurality of anchoring feet, and the redirecting blade are integrally formed as a unitary body.

### Claim 3

The wave deflector structure of claim 1, wherein at least one of the upper frame, the plurality of anchoring feet, and the redirecting blade is separately formed and connected to the lower frame.

### Claim 4

The wave deflector structure of claim 1, wherein each anchoring foot includes an aperture extending between an upper foot surface and the bottom foot surface, the aperture being configured to receive an anchor member.

### Claim 5

The wave deflector structure of claim 1, wherein the upper frame comprises first and second side support members and a transverse upper support member extending between the first and second side support members.

### Claim 6

The wave deflector structure of claim 5, wherein the redirecting blade is connected to the first and second side support members and to the transverse upper support member.

### Claim 7

The wave deflector structure of claim 1, wherein the front wave-facing surface of the redirecting blade is substantially planar.

### Claim 8

The wave deflector structure of claim 1, wherein the front wave-facing surface of the redirecting blade is curved.

### Claim 9

The wave deflector structure of claim 1, further comprising at least one brace having a first brace end connected to the lower frame and a second brace end connected to the upper frame.

### Claim 10

The wave deflector structure of claim 1, wherein the lower frame includes a first connector at the first lower-frame end and a second connector at the second lower-frame end, the first and second connectors being configured to connect the wave deflector structure to adjacent wave deflector structures.

### Claim 11

The wave deflector structure of claim 1, wherein the lower lower-frame surface is substantially planar and configured to rest on a shoreline support surface.

### Claim 12

The wave deflector structure of claim 1, wherein the plurality of anchoring feet extend laterally outwardly from the opposing lower-frame side surfaces.

### Claim 13

The wave deflector structure of claim 1, wherein the redirecting blade includes a lower edge adjacent the lower frame and an upper edge adjacent the upper upper-frame end.

### Claim 14

The wave deflector structure of claim 1, wherein the redirecting blade is removably connected to the upper frame.

### Claim 15

The wave deflector structure of claim 1, wherein the redirecting blade is welded, bolted, clamped, bonded, molded, or cast with the upper frame.

### Claim 16

A modular wave deflector system comprising:

a plurality of wave deflector structures arranged end-to-end, each wave deflector structure including:

a lower frame extending between opposing lower-frame ends;

an angled upper frame connected to and extending upwardly from the lower frame;

anchoring feet connected to the lower frame; and

a redirecting blade supported by the angled upper frame and having a wave-facing surface,

wherein the opposing lower-frame ends of adjacent wave deflector structures are connected together, and wherein the wave-facing surfaces of the redirecting blades cooperate to define a wave-redirecting barrier.

### Claim 17

The modular wave deflector system of claim 16, wherein adjacent redirecting blades include lateral blade ends that overlap one another.

### Claim 18

The modular wave deflector system of claim 16, wherein adjacent redirecting blades include lateral blade ends that abut one another.

### Claim 19

A wave deflector structure comprising:

a base frame having a bottom surface configured to face a support substrate and a top surface opposite the bottom surface;

an inclined blade-supporting frame connected to the base frame and extending upwardly at an angle from the top surface of the base frame;

a blade panel connected to the inclined blade-supporting frame, the blade panel having a water-facing surface and an opposite rear surface; and

anchor feet connected to the base frame and extending outwardly beyond at least one side surface of the base frame,

wherein the water-facing surface of the blade panel extends from a lower blade end toward an upper blade end along an inclined path to redirect water contacting the water-facing surface.

### Claim 20

The wave deflector structure of claim 19, wherein the base frame, the inclined blade-supporting frame, the anchor feet, and the blade panel comprise connected components of a corrosion-resistant marine structure.

---

## Additional Embodiment Wording

In certain embodiments, the lower frame defines a base portion and the anchoring feet define stabilizing portions extending from the base portion. The anchoring feet may be integral extensions of the lower frame such that no separate joint is present between the lower frame and the anchoring feet. Alternatively, the anchoring feet may be discrete members attached to exterior side surfaces or end surfaces of the lower frame.

The angled upper frame may be integral with the lower frame at a bend, molded junction, welded junction, cast junction, or reinforced joint. The upper frame may define a support plane and the redirecting blade may be disposed along the support plane. The redirecting blade may have a lower surface or lower edge positioned proximate the lower frame to reduce passage of water beneath the blade.

The redirecting blade may include a leading lower end that first receives incident wave flow and a trailing upper end over which redirected flow is discharged. The leading lower end may be rounded, chamfered, reinforced, thickened, or provided with a wear strip. The upper blade end may be straight, curved, flared, or provided with a lip configured to further direct water away from a protected side of the structure.

The rear surface of the redirecting blade may face a protected region. The upper frame may be positioned adjacent the rear surface to support the blade against wave loading applied to the front surface. The blade may be continuous between the opposing lateral blade ends, or may include a plurality of blade segments connected to the upper frame.

The anchoring feet may be positioned so that loads applied to the blade are transferred through the upper frame into the lower frame and from the lower frame into the anchoring feet. The anchoring feet may distribute such loads over the support surface and may cooperate with anchors to resist sliding, uplift, rotation, and overturning of the wave deflector structure.
